Baby AB

By: Kate Barry | Paid

Proposal


Show:

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Meet Dewald Brevis - cricket's new superstar

Unique Selling Point:
A one-on-one with Dewald Brevis who has just returned from his debut season in the IPL.
We take him back to his primary school where he played only 5 years ago. The 2000 pupils of Laërskool Hennopspark have a special surprise planned for their hero and we're invited.
We also meet his first coach Eddie Naidoo at Laudium Cricket Club where Brevis played from the age of 9, his High school coach Deon Botes, and his Titans coach Mandla Mashimbyi.


Summary:
Sitting in the front row of the photograph of the Affies first cricket team, smiling broadly, is the cheerful, open face of Dewald Brevis who has exploded onto the international cricket scene like a comet.
Just 6 months ago he was studying for his matric exams at Afrikaanse Hoër Seunskool in Pretoria. Now he’s earning 6 figures in the Indian Premier League cricket championship. He’s been dubbed “Baby AB” because of the remarkable resemblance of his batting style to that of former Protea’s star AB de Villiers – another Affies alumni. But the experts warn that Brevis’s talent far exceeds that of de Villiers at the same age. He turned 19 last month.




Further information:
We trace the extraordinary career of the most extraordinary cricket talent to come out of South Africa in a generation.
Having cut his teeth on Club Cricket in Laudium at the age of 9, Brevis shone at both primary and high school. He played for Titans Under 11 teams and was snapped up by the Titans senior provincial side while in Grade 12. He matriculated in 2021, and in January 2022 he played for South Africa in the 2022 ICC Under-19 Cricket World Cup in the West Indies. He excelled again, scoring two centuries and three fifties, and was named the Player of the Tournament after a record-breaking 506 runs.

In February 2022 he was bought by the Mumbai Indians in the Indian Premier League Auction for R6 million. He has quickly proved himself with a sensational knock against the Punjab Kings, smashing 4, 6, 6, 6, 6 in a single over.
Watch it here: https://www.iplt20.com/video/42734/46666---dewald-brevis-smashes-rahul-chahar

Veterans of the game have been raving about him on Twitter:

Michael Vaughan: “Dewald Brevis!! Best young player I have seen…

Mark Waugh: “Wow unbelievable ball striking and presence at the crease for such a young batsman. #freakish

His stint with the Mumbai Indians was also an intense learning experience for Brevis. The head coach is Mahela Jayawardene, and the batting mentor is The Little Master himself: Sachin Tendulkar. Brevis is also a decent bowler and promises to be a phenomenal all-rounder like Jacques Kallis.

We will have access to photographs of his career from an early age, as well as all Supersport footage of his provincial, national and professional career. All his coaches - from Laudium, Hennopspark, Affies and Titans have agreed to interviews, as well as his brother and best friend, Reinardt.

Script:


BABY AB SCRIPT

Sfx: Ah this one’s gone all the way – beautiful strike from Brevis. Baby AB with an AB-type shot.

V/O: It’s the stuff that dreams are made of. From schoolboy to superstar in one season.

SFX: He’s gone again!

V/O: Meet Dewald Brevis, the teenage batsman who knocked the socks off the cricketing world at the Indian Premier League.

Sfx: Ah, here we go again! Short this time, smashed away. Three on the bounce.
Ah you devil Brevis!

Sfx: Oh and another one! Unbelievable scenes from Brevis. The biggest of the lot to finish the over. Four sixes on the bounce, 29 from the over.

V/O: It’s been a meteoric rise to fame and fortune for the boy from Centurion who wrote matric just last year.

Dewald: It has always been my dream to be in this position, but it has happened very quickly and I’m very grateful for it.

Deon: You know as a 19-year-old to go to the IPL and he actually looks like he should be there, I think that is quite a big achievement.

V/O: Head of Sport Deon Botes coached both Dewald and AB de Villiers.

Deon: AB was one of those guys that really hit the on-drive Under 14-boy. You could see it, so Dewald had those characteristics already when we saw him for the first time.

V/O: But Dewald had already perfected that shot at primary school in Hennops Park. And this week they welcomed him home with huge fanfare.

Sfx: Hero’s welcome in school hall.

Dewald: To have children that’s going crazy, like that’s very special. To make their day and spend time with them is really the ultimate.

Link: So this is where it all began – Laërskool Hennopspark. And when Dewald Brevis arrived here he got a hero’s welcome. It’s hard to think that just 5 years ago, he was one of them.

Dewald: Ja, dis ek!

Juan: He’s actually a game changer. That’s the reason why I picked him in Grade 6 for the first team.

V/O: Coach Juan Parsons has known him since Grade 1.

Juan: From six years old he was actually into sports a lot. If he can play cricket, tennis, hockey then Dewald was there.

V/O: And it seems he was equally talented in all of them. He even played rugby for the Bulls Under 12 and 13 sides but gave it up for hockey in high school.

Dewald: It literally goes hand to hand with cricket because playing a reverse sweep is the same as hitting a back stick.

V/O: His family have always been hugely supportive and built practice nets in the back garden for him. Fortunately, his older brother Reinardt is a fast bowler.

Mac: But was he always hitting you for a six?

Reinardt: Well I must say I did get him a couple of times out, but as he grew older it became more difficult and I became more frustrated.

Sfx: Dewald op 99, eerste game vir Laudium Klub onder 13.

V/O: But Dewald has always punched above his weight. He scored this century for his club side when he was only 11.

Eddie: When he arrived here, you would never say that he was from outside the way he mixed with the other boys. They all became friends very, very early. And in fact, everybody in the team loved him.

V/O: Eddie Naidoo coached Dewald from the age of 10 at Laudium Cricket Club near Pretoria.

Eddie: You know what, when they say talent comes from God, Dewald had it in him already. You could see at a young age this boy was going to go places.

V/O: Dewald made the Affies First Team in Grade 9, but the Covid lockdown meant he missed two cricket seasons. Luckily he had the back yard nets.

Deon: We had some training sessions there we had to drive through, I think AB did a session or two there as well.

Dewald: That was great! I can remember like whenever my mom went out to maybe get groceries, then the first thing when the gate closes, me and my brother take the stumps, everything outside. And then we would play, and then we wait ‘til we hear a car or something. Then we would go back into...

Mac: And then you act like you’ve been working?

Dewald: Exactly! And then my mom said what have you been doing? No we’ve been working, and then we said as she’s in the house – Mom, can we take a break please? So then the game just goes on.

V/O: While he was in matric Dewald was signed by the Titans senior side - at the age of 18. Coach Mandla Mashimbyi also played a part in his early development.

Mandla: Dewald is a special player and we felt that it’s good for us to invest in him at this age because he will go on and become a force in cricket. Because if we didn’t take him I can pretty much assure you that somebody else would have come for him.

V/O: And inevitably he was selected to represent South Africa at the ICC Under19 World Cup in January this year.

Dewald: For me that’s the biggest dream, to put that green and gold over your head. Because as a young boy when they sing the anthem I would also stand and close my eyes and see myself on the field at Lords or wherever, and how I sing that and how I turn my head and see the crowds around me.

V/O: South Africa didn’t win the trophy but Dewald smashed all batting records and won player of the tournament.

Sfx: That is simply magnificent!

Dewald: I want to go out there and I want to show the world and the people who I am.

V/O: And that opportunity came in February when he was bought at the IPL Auction by the Mumbai Indians for R6 million.

Link: Is he worth R6 million? Let’s find out………. Oh! He can hit a ball!

Mac: Six million rand! What is the first thing you bought?

Dewald: The first thing I didn’t touch the money. I haven’t touched the money still. I just want to stay Dewald Brevis and to just play cricket because I love it.

V/O: In March he packed his bags, said goodbye to his dog, and was driven to the airport by his parents. He flew First Class to Mumbai where he was welcomed by the wealthiest franchise in the League. He was only 18 and about to face his lifelong heroes - like Virat Kohli, the ICC Cricketer of the Decade.

Dewald: It was overwhelming at sometimes. like meeting Virat. I couldn’t get a word out. I was literally standing there. He asked me – How are you and everything? I was just, I’m good. It was so special.

V/O: But even more special was the first ball Dewald ever bowled in the IPL.

Dewald: That ball that I bowled for Virat – when I released the ball - literally everything felt perfect from that delivery.

Sfx: Oh hello! Big appeal. Given!

V/O: He got Virat Kohli out lbw.

Dewald: It was so great. It felt like a wicket in the moment, like for the team. But later on you realize when the DRS comes on, like the reviewing system, you realize this is Virat!

Sfx: Been given! Kohli doesn’t like it.

V/O: But other cricketing icons raved about him.

Dewald: My ultimate goal is to play for the Proteas in all three formats.

V/O: It’s unlikely that he’ll be chosen for the T20 World Cup in October, but that won’t deter him.

Mandla: I think his hunger, his hunger to be the best that’s what makes him Dewald. If that is looked after this kid will go on and just improve and become probably one of the best cricketers the world has ever seen.

Having cut his teeth on Club Cricket in Laudium at the age of 9, Brevis shone at both primary and high school. He played for Titans Under 11 teams and was snapped up by the Titans senior provincial side while in Grade 12. He matriculated in 2021, and in January 2022 he played for South Africa in the 2022 ICC Under-19 Cricket World Cup in the West Indies. He excelled again, scoring two centuries and three fifties, and was named the Player of the Tournament after a record-breaking 506 runs. In February 2022 he was bought by the Mumbai Indians in the Indian Premier League Auction for R6 million. He has quickly proved himself with a sensational knock against the Punjab Kings, smashing 4, 6, 6, 6, 6 in a single over. Watch it here: https://www.iplt20.com/video/42734/46666---dewald-brevis-smashes-rahul-chahar Veterans of the game have been raving about him on Twitter: Michael Vaughan: “Dewald Brevis!! Best young player I have seen… Mark Waugh: “Wow unbelievable ball striking and presence at the crease for such a young batsman. #freakish His stint with the Mumbai Indians was also an intense learning experience for Brevis. The head coach is Mahela Jayawardene, and the batting mentor is The Little Master himself: Sachin Tendulkar. Brevis is also a decent bowler and promises to be a phenomenal all-rounder like Jacques Kallis. We will have access to photographs of his career from an early age, as well as all Supersport footage of his provincial, national and professional career. All his coaches - from Laudium, Hennopspark, Affies and Titans have agreed to interviews, as well as his brother and best friend, Reinardt.
